newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil oil imports rise on price expectations.
newsitem.headline: Brazil oil imports rise on price expectations.

text.p: Brazilian state oil monopoly Petrobras increased oil imports in September in anticipation of rising world oil prices, the company president said.
"We bought up a position in September anticipating that international prices will continue rising given the conflicts in Iraq," said Joel Mendes Renno at a press conference in Rio de Janeiro.
Petrobras imports around 43-44 percent of Brazil's oil demand.

Brazil's Finance Ministry partly blamed last month's surge in oil imports for a larger-than-expected September trade deficit, prompting speculation that Petrobras was stocking up ahead of an expected oilworkers strike.
However, Renno dismissed the possibility of a strike, saying the company was "absolutely not" expecting any strike action.
The company and the United Oilworkers Federation have clashed in recent weeks in their annual round of talks over pay rises and job guarantees.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
